subject: Re: Live inference pause cascade — executive briefing
messages:
From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@krescenthealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: platform@krescenthealth.com, procurement@krescenthealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Production pause — live transcripts stopped mid-stream

Jonas —

We saw our production live-transcription sessions drop to silent chunks today around 13:45 PST. The UI shows the websocket connection still open, but tokens stop flowing for ~8–20s then resume. This is happening across three clinical pods and affects patient-facing transcripts, so clinicians are losing context.

We escalated to PagerDuty but wanted to make you aware directly. Our side shows retries and chunked-transfer resets on the ELB before the Redwood upstream. Can someone confirm whether this was a capacity spike, a routing fallback, or a streaming runtime failure?

Attaching logs we pulled. Please advise next steps and ETA for root cause.

—Alice
Director, Platform Engineering
Krescent Health

Attachments: krescent_incident_logs_20261110.tar.gz

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@krescenthealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production pause — live transcripts stopped mid-stream

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're treating this as a high-priority incident. Quick notes from initial triage:
- We see a correlated increase in 502/504s from the edge proxies around the same timestamps.
- Some requests show chunked-encoding keepalive frames being ACKed by the proxy but no body chunks forwarded for ~10s.
- The runtime metrics show a small spike in model-queue length on the region pool but not enough to explain 10–20s silences.

I'm pulling in Marissa (runtime) and Rishi (routing/fallbacks). We'll run a trace to see where the pipe is being held. Can you confirm whether you were on Dedicated or Hosted during the incident and if you had any traffic shaping changes?

I'll follow up with a timeline and a proposed mitigations plan within 2 hours.

—Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production pause — live transcripts stopped mid-stream

Triage notes (runtime):
- Replayed Krescent traces in staging; reproduced chunked pauses when we introduced a simultaneous warmup job that caused KV-cache thrashing.
- Evidence points to a combo: (1) prefix/KV cache eviction spikes causing backend compute stalls; (2) edge proxy (ELB) TCP window/idle heuristics closing or batching frames causing delayed body forwarding.
- There is also one suspicious error pattern where our streaming worker's backpressure timer resets but does not emit a connection-level heartbeat, leaving clients with open WS but no tokens.

Immediate mitigations suggested:
1) Patch runtime to emit periodic heartbeat frames at socket-level when in-flight tokens are queued (hotfix, 2–4 hours deploy).
2) Short-term: auto-fail streaming requests to a non-streaming fallback for affected routes (config toggle) — this reduces UX but keeps customers online.
3) Edge: request Krescent to whitelist longer idle at ELB or move to TCP keepalive of 15s until hotfix deploys.

I'll start a hotfix branch and run a canary. Rishi — can you confirm whether routing fallbacks were triggered?

—Marissa
Senior Runtime Engineer

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production pause — live transcripts stopped mid-stream

Routing notes:
- Policy routing did trigger an elastic fallback from the region pool to a cross-region replica for ~27s at 13:46:11; that matches a short window of higher latency. The fallback logic attempted to maintain streaming mode but opened a TCP proxied path that traversed an intermediate NAT/ELB pair.
- The cross-region path introduces a small MTU/path-MTU behaviour with chunk coalescing; combined with ELB idle heuristics it can produce the observed 8–20s effective silence before buffered chunks flush.
- We did NOT see quota exhaustion or model OOMs.

Action for routing: pin Krescent to a single AZ pool for customer-specific routing until runtime heartbeat is out. Also pushing a feature flag to force non-streaming on fallback paths for critical accounts.

—Rishi
Head of Serving Reliability

From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@krescenthealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: platform@krescenthealth.com, procurement@krescenthealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production pause — live transcripts stopped mid-stream

Jonas/Team —

Thanks for the rapid investigation. Krescent is on Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 with a pinned AZ, but we do run a small DR route that kicks in automatically on node failures. We can temporarily disable the DR cross-region failover on our side for the next 24h if that helps.

Two asks from our side:
1) We need a short executive summary for our CIO; she wants to understand impact (sessions affected, minutes of silence) and whether SLA credits will be considered.
2) ETA on the runtime heartbeat hotfix and whether Redwood will perform a retroactive log analysis for postmortem.

If you prefer a quick call, I can make time at 10:00am tomorrow.

—Alice

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Tan <alice.tan@krescenthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production pause — live transcripts stopped mid-stream — executive briefing

Executive briefing (for CIO & internal execs):
- Incident summary: between 13:44–13:53 PST on 2026-11-10 Krescent Health observed intermittent streaming silence across 3 pods; median silence ~9s, max observed 22s. Affected estimated sessions: 47 active live-transcription sessions (0.6% of Krescent's peak). Error rate spike: 502/504 increased by 3.2x during the window.
- Root cause (probable): a failover-induced cross-region routing path combined with runtime KV-cache eviction causing transient compute stalls; ELB/TCP-level batching and idle heuristics amplified token delivery gaps.
- Immediate mitigations completed: disabled cross-region DR routing for Krescent (customer toggle), pushed config to force non-streaming fallback on cross-region paths, and deployed a canary heartbeat hotfix to streaming worker (canary at 10% traffic).
- Next steps / owner assignments:
  * Marissa — finish hotfix rollout to 100% and validate with synthetic long-lived streams (ETA: +6h from this message).
  * Rishi — complete routing pin (customer-scoped) and add a fallback flag to gate streaming on non-local paths (ETA: +3h).
  * Jonas — produce a postmortem draft with timeline and SLA impact; coordinate executive summary for Krescent CIO (ETA: EOD 2026-11-13).

SLA and credits: we will evaluate per contract. Jonas, please sync with sales/finance and provide an initial impact calc by EOD.

Cc'ing Alice to close the loop; we propose the 10:00am call as requested if the CIO wants direct Q&A.

—Lauren
VP, Customer Reliability & Escalations
Redwood Inference
